ctx.x: That's right, because there was a lot of drinking, and you know, they usually put them in the woods. Before that I used to play with Red Calhoun in Dallas, Texas. He played a lot of clarinet. I was playing drums with him, and we used to play at a road house, black road house, in Dallas, Texas, in a place called Elm Thicket, and so these road houses were very popular. People could go out there and these -- this was back in the woods where -- way out. Nobody
couldn't distrub the peace, or anything.
